A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gaussian Splatting Lucas-Kanade by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original novel-view synthesis experiments, quantitative benchmark comparisons, component ablations, and qualitative motion and reconstruction analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds DyCheck evaluations, quantitative supervision comparisons, prior-sensitivity experiments, and a controlled synthetic uncertainty demonstration.

M1.justification: Equation (6) changes the reported photometric objective from squared L2 error to absolute error. The core deformation network, pseudoinverse-based positional and rotational velocities, time integration, and depth-ranking regularization remain intact. This is a limited change in the stated objective, without evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V2 adds five handheld monocular DyCheck scenes and a controlled synthetic scene with randomized ball positions. These extend evaluation to harder camera-motion conditions and deliberately inconsistent temporal observations. The Dynamic Scenes, Plenoptic Videos, HyperNeRF, and DAVIS coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds MA-GS to the Plenoptic comparison in Table 4, Marbles to the new DyCheck comparison, and a jointly depth-and-flow-supervised DeformableGS control in Table 3. The existing Dynamic Scenes and HyperNeRF comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce original-pose versus pose-refined DyCheck settings, alternative depth/flow priors, and a synthetic control contrasting randomized red/green ball positions with a temporally consistent blue ball. Existing benchmark metrics and documented training settings are retained; the pose-refinement procedure is only briefly described.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Table 3 quantifies direct depth/flow supervision, Appendix A.3 tests sensitivity to alternative prior estimators, and Figure A6 examines Jacobian-based uncertainty under inconsistent observations. The original component ablation remains as Table 6, and the earlier trajectory and initialization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3 and Figure A6 newly report a qualitative per-Gaussian uncertainty proxy based on deformation Jacobians. This is limited uncertainty reporting: neither version supplies repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or calibration of the proxy.

E6.justification: V2 adds DyCheck scores, MA-GS results, direct-supervision results, and prior-sensitivity findings. For example, the Playground study reports PSNR 26.96 with Depth Anything V2 and 27.04 with MemFlow, versus 26.34 for the original setup. Shared entries in v1 Tables 1–4 are retained in v2 Tables 1 and 4–6. Pose-refined DyCheck scores represent an additional setting, not a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 newly states a small-motion assumption and invokes a Taylor expansion. V2 also revises the velocity identities from v1 Equations (9)–(10), including removal of the final spatial-derivative equality in v1 Equation (10). These are limited changes to assumptions and mathematical reasoning; no substantial new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central claims about analytical continuous-time regularization, improved dynamic geometry, and avoiding additional learnable parameters remain. V2's introduction explicitly conditions the Lucas-Kanade adaptation on a small-motion constraint, providing a limited qualification of the claimed derivation.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning overfitting from direct supervision, visual-versus-quantitative tradeoffs among depth/flow priors, camera-pose accuracy, and Jacobians as uncertainty indicators. The existing limitations concerning SfM initialization, camera calibration, and computational cost remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page link and specifies Monte Carlo integration using ten sample points per domain. Existing hardware, optimizer, learning rates, warm-up schedules, and motion-mask threshold remain documented as before. The new Monte Carlo statement coexists with the retained Runge-Kutta description, leaving the precise solver procedure ambiguous.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for Marbles, Shape of Motion, MiDaS, Depth Anything V2, FlowNet, and MemFlow. It also explicitly credits Flow-supervised NeRF's role in analytical flow supervision. These extend the existing positioning without substantially replacing its related-work framework.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of Sections 3–4 are rewritten, including the Gaussian-mean notation, motion decomposition, and velocity explanation. The evaluation narrative is reorganized and expanded with dedicated supervision comparisons. This is extensive editorial revision despite retaining the overall section sequence.

P2.justification: V2 adds two main-text tables and three appendix figures, expands the Plenoptic table, moves Figure 1 onto the opening page, and exchanges the order of the pipeline and trajectory figures. Conference formatting and widespread resizing and relocation further change the presentation; retained appendix illustrations are identifiable across renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation through quantitative direct-supervision comparisons, alternative-prior tests, and harder DyCheck evaluations, while explicitly stating the small-motion assumption. These gains are tempered by underdescribed pose-refinement comparisons and the conflicting Runge-Kutta/Monte Carlo description. The additions provide a useful but limited net improvement in evidential support and documentation.
